title: Burst lease allocator and tenant guardrails — notebook
body:
Purpose:
This is a working notebook for a product experiment and ops playbook that combines a small-lease burst allocator (time-boxed burst tokens) with tenant-level guardrails to protect isolation. Aim: let tenants temporarily exceed base reservation for short windows (bursts) while ensuring predictable degradation and fast remediation if noisy behavior threatens SLOs.

Context / motivation:
- We have many PRDs already focused on big autoscalers and long-lived reservations. This doc sketches a complementary lightweight mechanism for short-lived demand spikes where autoscale is too slow or too expensive.
- Observed patterns: scheduled campaigns and unpredictable user spikes that last 1–15 minutes and cause noisy neighbors. Full autoscale ramp/scale-down costs too much and adds latency.
- Target: 95th pct latency SLOs for medium/large customers, allow controlled micro-bursts for growth-stage customers without compromising isolation for enterprise tenants.

High-level idea:
1) Burst leases: allocate a small time-boxed "lease" (e.g., 10s/30s/5min) that grants a tenant a fixed number of ephemeral slots or a temporary throughput multiplier. Leases are consumable and decay over a short horizon.
2) Guardrails: enforce per-tenant soft and hard limits (soft = warned/telemetry, hard = triggered fallback) and cross-tenant isolation signals (pool-wide headroom, thermals, per-GPU load).
3) Graceful fallback: on hard-limit breach route to cheaper model variant or queued latency lane with exponential backoff and hold a small credit to avoid immediate retries.

Success metrics (initial):
- Reduce tail-latency incidents caused by microbursts by >= 65% in pilot pool (compare baseline month).
- Keep percent of requests served by fallback < 2% for enterprise-tier pools.
- Mean cost delta of enabling burst leases < +8% for pilot tenants (target to be lowered).

API / config sketch (developer-facing):
- Lease request call: POST /v1/dedicated/tenants/{tid}/burst-lease request body: {"lease_duration_sec": 30, "slot_count": 4, "reason": "campaign"}
- Server returns: {"granted": true, "lease_id": "L-1234", "expires_at": "2025-02-11T14:05:10Z", "variant": "A100-q4", "notes": "soft-guardrail-active"}
- Admin knobs: max_simultaneous_leases, per-tenant-burst-budget-per-day, hard_quota_threshold_pct

Config example (operator-oriented YAML):
---
burst_pool: pool-us-west-2-a
max_leases_per_pool: 32
per_tenant_daily_budget_slots: 120
default_lease_duration_sec: 60
soft_quota_pct: 70  # emit telemetry when tenant uses >70% of daily budget
hard_quota_pct: 95  # deny new leases after this threshold
pool_headroom_warn_pct: 20  # warn when pool headroom < 20%
pool_headroom_hard_pct: 8   # stop granting leases under this
---

Simulation plan (short):
- Build a lightweight discrete-event sim that models 200 tenants, with 10 spike-heavy tenants and rest baseline. Variables: burst arrival rate, lease durations, pool size, thermal events.
- Run grid of scenarios to find safe defaults for max_leases_per_pool and per_tenant_daily_budget_slots.
- Target metric: fraction of scenarios where enterprise tenant 95th-latency remains within SLO.

Operational playbook (ops-run):
- Alerting: create two alerts tied to the feature:
  * burst-pool-headroom-critical (trigger when pool_headroom_hard_pct breached for >30s) -> Pager to SRE, auto-disable lease grants in that pool.
  * tenant-burst-abuse-warning (trigger when tenant consumes > 50% daily budget in 10m window) -> create CS ticket and throttle new leases for that tenant.
- Runbook steps for headroom-critical:
 1) Check pool telemetry: GPU utilization, thermal logs, KV cache size.
 2) Disable lease grants: set grant_enabled=false for affected pool via operator console.
 3) Initiate graceful fallback: for impacted tenants switch to fallback-route (cheaper model) for 5min, incrementally re-enable if headroom returns.
 4) Post-incident: run root-cause and tag tenant events for billing/credits.

Experiments to run (MVP):
- Pilot group: 8 tenants (mix of mid-market & enterprise) in a single 4-GPU pool.
- Experiment variants: A) leases enabled with soft_guardrails; B) leases+aggressive hard_guardrails; C) leases disabled (control).
- Duration: 4 weeks (2w ramp + 2w measurement).
- Measurement: latency SLO breaches, percent fallbacks, nightly cost delta, CS escalations.

Open questions / risks:
- Behavioral: will tenants code to request many tiny leases to game the system? Need anti-abuse (cooldown per-tenant, costing).
- Economic: how to bill leases? Charge per slot-second or embed into request unit price?
- Complexity: adds many fast-path checks in runtime—can we keep latency overhead < 2%?
- Thermal/heterogeneous hardware: how to map leases across varied GPU types and quantized models?

Mitigations considered:
- Rate-limit per-tenant lease requests and require a token bucket tied to billing commitments.
- Small stub in runtime for lease check that is O(1) and cached at routing layer to avoid per-request DB hits.
- Prefer local pool headroom checks rather than global to reduce coordination.

Notes / divergent thoughts (brainstorm fragments):
- Instead of slots, consider "CPU-style" priority tickets (weight) that can be fractionally consumed by requests; harder to reason about but smoother.
- Could be combined with prefix/KV caching credits: a tenant with warm KV could get larger effective burst without extra GPUs.
- Use ML model to predict short spikes and pre-grant leases to trusted tenants (pre-warm tokens).

Next steps (immediate):
- Align with infra lead on simulation runner scope: @Liam (Linear: REDW-4123).
- Prototype a minimal grant-service with in-memory lease ledger and operator flags (1 engineer, 2 weeks).
- Prepare pilot tenant invites and legal note for billing experiment.

Appendix: quick checklist for prototype rollout:
- [ ] Sim harness implemented and initial runs executed
- [ ] Grant-service basic API and operator toggle implemented
- [ ] Alerting rules created in Grafana/Alertmanager
- [ ] Pilot tenants onboarded + consented to fallback policy
- [ ] Post-mortem template prepared

Unresolved decisions to pick before alpha:
- Billing model (slot-second vs included in reserved commit)
- Granularity of lease (slot vs multiplier vs priority credit)
- Default parameters (max_leases_per_pool, daily budgets)

Raw links and refs (working):
- Linear ticket: https://linear.app/REDW/issue/REDW-4123
- Infra prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/827
- SRE runbook template: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/REDW/Dedicated+Capacity+Playbooks

Notes to self:
- Keep this doc experimental: capture sims and pilot telemetry here, then convert to a formal PRD if metrics look good.
- Try to avoid reusing the term "burst credits" in customer docs; call it "time-boxed leases" to set expectation of ephemeral nature.
summary: Working notebook proposing time-boxed burst leases with tenant guardrails: design sketches, sim plan, ops playbook, API sketch, unresolved questions and immediate next steps.
